label: prf:frobenius-s-classification
title: Proof of frobenius s classification
html:
Each S-eigenvalue is checked in turn.

Coefficients. The action q \mapsto q^{-1} extends to the underlying field of fractions and acts on each coefficient:

  • D = q^4 + 4q^2 + 1 is palindromic in q^2: under q \to q^{-1}, D \to q^{-4} + 4q^{-2} + 1 = q^{-4}(1 + 4q^2 + q^4) = q^{-4} D. Then W_{\mathrm{sym}} = q^2/D \to q^{-2}/(q^{-4} D) = q^2/D, invariant. Same for W_{\mathrm{alt}}. For W_{\mathrm{std}}: (q^2+1)^2 \to (q^{-2}+1)^2 = q^{-4}(1+q^2)^2, so W_{\mathrm{std}} \to q^{-4}(1+q^2)^2 / (q^{-4} D) = W_{\mathrm{std}}.
  • [3]_q = q^2 + 1 + q^{-2}: invariant under q \to q^{-1}.
  • h_{\mathrm{A}} = q - q^{-1} \to q^{-1} - q = -h_{\mathrm{A}}, so h_{\mathrm{A}} has eigenvalue -1 and h_{\mathrm{A}}^2 has eigenvalue +1.
  • z: at the canonical weight z = q^3/(q^2+1) the action gives z \mapsto 1/(q(q^2+1)) = z - h_{\mathrm{A}}, the negative-crossing loop value \mathrm{tr}_M(\sigma^{-1}). So z is not an S-eigenvector: S exchanges the two loop values. Equivalently, the Markov trace commutes with S, \mathrm{tr}_M(S(X)) = S(\mathrm{tr}_M(X)), and the relation z(q^{-1}) = z(q) - h_{\mathrm{A}} is exactly the condition for this.
  • Catalan's constant G, Borromean volume 8G, electron mass m_e, and binding scale \alpha are real canonical constants unaffected by the algebraic action.

Functional \Phi_2. The transfer matrix is T(c, d) = \begin{pmatrix} ch_{\mathrm{A}} + d & c \\ c & d \end{pmatrix} with \det T = d(ch_{\mathrm{A}} + d) - c^2. The Frobenius antipode maps the primitive factor (c, d) to (\bar c, \bar d - \bar c h_{\mathrm{A}}), where the bar is q \mapsto q^{-1} on the coefficients (this swaps \sigma \leftrightarrow \sigma^{-1} and inverts q; without barring the coefficients, ud = (1, -h_{\mathrm{A}}/2) would map to (1, -3h_{\mathrm{A}}/2) rather than to itself). See Table 3.

For each primitive the determinant is S-invariant. Since \det is multiplicative on chain products, \Phi_2 = \sum_i \log\lvert\det M_i\rvert is S-invariant.

Functional \Phi_3. Write an element of the two-strand Hecke algebra as X = c\,\sigma + d, with characters \chi^{\mathrm{sym}}(X) = cq + d and \chi^{\mathrm{alt}}(X) = -c q^{-1} + d (the eigenvalues q and -q^{-1} of \sigma). The bar involution sends \sigma \mapsto \sigma^{-1} = \sigma - h_{\mathrm{A}} and q \mapsto q^{-1}, so S(c\sigma + d) = \bar c\,\sigma + (\bar d - \bar c\,h_{\mathrm{A}}), where \bar{\ } is q \mapsto q^{-1} on the coefficients. It is a ring automorphism (semilinear over q \mapsto q^{-1}), so S of a chain product is the product of the barred factors.

Call X bar-homogeneous of sign \varepsilon \in \{\pm 1\} if \bar c = \varepsilon c and \bar d = -\varepsilon d. Two facts follow by direct expansion, using \bar h_{\mathrm{A}} = -h_{\mathrm{A}} and q - h_{\mathrm{A}} = q^{-1}:

  1. Character swap. If X is homogeneous of sign \varepsilon, then \chi^{\mathrm{sym}}(S X) = \varepsilon c\,(q - h_{\mathrm{A}}) - \varepsilon d = -\varepsilon\,\chi^{\mathrm{alt}}(X) and \chi^{\mathrm{alt}}(S X) = -\varepsilon c\,(q^{-1} + h_{\mathrm{A}}) - \varepsilon d = -\varepsilon\,\chi^{\mathrm{sym}}(X).
  2. Closure. With \sigma^2 = h_{\mathrm{A}}\sigma + 1, (a\sigma + b)(c\sigma + d) = (ac\,h_{\mathrm{A}} + ad + bc)\,\sigma + (ac + bd). If the factors are homogeneous of signs \varepsilon, \varepsilon', every monomial of the \sigma-coefficient has bar-sign -\varepsilon\varepsilon' and every monomial of the constant term has bar-sign \varepsilon\varepsilon', so the product is homogeneous of sign -\varepsilon\varepsilon'.

The three primitives (1, 0), (1, -h_{\mathrm{A}}), (1, -h_{\mathrm{A}}/2) are homogeneous of sign +1 (the coefficient 1 is bar-invariant and 0, -h_{\mathrm{A}}, -h_{\mathrm{A}}/2 are bar-anti-invariant), and the unit (0, 1) is homogeneous of sign -1. By closure every chain product X_i entering \Phi_3 is homogeneous, of sign (-1)^{n-1} for n primitive factors, and by the character swap

  \frac{\chi^{\mathrm{sym}}(S X_i)}{\chi^{\mathrm{alt}}(S X_i)}
  = \frac{-\varepsilon\,\chi^{\mathrm{alt}}(X_i)}{-\varepsilon\,\chi^{\mathrm{sym}}(X_i)}
  = \left(\frac{\chi^{\mathrm{sym}}(X_i)}{\chi^{\mathrm{alt}}(X_i)}\right)^{-1}.

The sign \varepsilon cancels, so only homogeneity matters, not the parity of n. The identity holds in the field of rational functions and so at every evaluation point where both characters are nonzero. Taking \log\lvert\cdot\rvert and summing over i gives \Phi_3(S(\beta)) = -\Phi_3(\beta), eigenvalue -1. (The argument holds over a generic field.)

Scope. The argument is for chains of bar-homogeneous factors, which includes every chain of the three primitives (and the nucleon and electron crossings of the same form). It is not a property of \Phi_3 on all of the Hecke algebra. For a general element, \chi^{\mathrm{sym}} and \chi^{\mathrm{alt}} are bar-equivariant, since both are ring homomorphisms and \chi(\sigma^{-1}) = \overline{\chi(\sigma)}. So S acts on \Phi_3, as on \Phi_1, by the evaluation flip q_0 \mapsto q_0^{-1}, which is not a sign change in general. Example: X = \sigma + 1 is not homogeneous, and the product of the two ratios is -(q+1)^2/(q-1)^2 \neq \pm 1, so \Phi_3 + \Phi_3 \circ S picks up 2\log\lvert (q_0+1)/(q_0-1) \rvert \neq 0 from this factor. Numerically, one finds \lvert\Phi_3 + \Phi_3 \circ S\rvert \lesssim 10^{-51} at the proton pin (mpmath, 50 digits) on all seven of its chains.

Functional \Phi_1. Because the canonical Markov trace commutes with S, S acts on \Phi_1 by inverting the evaluation point: \Phi_1(S(\beta); q_0) = \Phi_1(\beta; q_0^{-1}). The raw \Phi_1 is therefore not an S-eigenvector. It splits as \Phi_1 = \Phi_1^{+} + \Phi_1^{-} with \Phi_1^{\pm} = \tfrac12\bigl(\Phi_1(\beta) \pm \Phi_1(S(\beta))\bigr); the eigenvalue +1 in Table 1 is that of the projection \Phi_1^{+}, which is S-even by construction, and \Phi_1^{-} is S-odd. \square

Corollary. Since \Phi_2 is S-even and \Phi_3 is S-odd,

  \mathfrak{m}(S(\beta)) - \mathfrak{m}(\beta)
  = -2 \alpha \bigl(\Phi_1^{-}(\beta) + h_{\mathrm{A}}^2 \Phi_3(\beta)\bigr).

The chirality term is the unique S-odd channel only when \Phi_1^{-} vanishes. It does not vanish in general: on the proton chain uud at the proton pin, \Phi_1^{-} \approx 0.0526 against h_{\mathrm{A}}^2 \Phi_3 \approx 0.00912, a ratio \approx 5.77.

Since S maps the proton braid (uud) to a braid with quark content (ddu), the S-odd part of the mass is the structural carrier of the proton-neutron splitting at the Wedderburn formula level, and it has two sources, \Phi_1^{-} and h_{\mathrm{A}}^2\Phi_3, not one.
